_comment: Lint ratchet baseline. Checked by scripts/lint-ratchet.mjs from the CI
`lint` job: the count may fall, never rise. See CI-LINT-PLAN.md.
`fatals` is tracked separately, and ratcheted separately, because a fatal
is a PARSE failure rather than a rule finding — the file was not linted at
all, so it contributes zero errors and looks clean by the only number the
ratchet would otherwise read. Both workspaces are at 0 and must stay there.
The backend sat at 120 fatals until Phase 4: tsconfig.json excludes
src/**/__tests__/** and src/**/*.test.ts, and a file outside
parserOptions.project is a fatal, not a skip, so every test file failed to
parse. backend/.eslintrc.json now points at tsconfig.eslint.json, which
extends the production config and drops only those two excludes. The
production tsconfig.json is untouched, so nothing changed about what is
emitted to dist/. Admitting 120 files is what took backend errors/warnings
from 5658/277 to 6293/408 — a deliberate re-baseline, not a regression.
Phase 5 then began bringing it down for real: the first pass typed three
DB/Mongo boundary files and took errors 6293 -> 6062; the second removed
268 redundant `(req as any).user` casts, which alone took 6062 -> 4808.
the third typed the GenieACS device document, 4808 -> 4700.
the fourth narrowed req.body in secgw-controller, 4700 -> 4474.
the fifth did the same for gsm-controller, 4474 -> 4398.
the sixth typed the FRR/iproute2 command-output parsers, 4398 -> 4289, and
the seventh wrapped the 51 async route handlers that had no try/catch at
all, 4289 -> 4223. That last one is a BUG FIX, not a typing change: those
handlers leaked a rejection to Express and the request hung with no reply.
An eighth caught 7 more of the same defect in handlers that DID have a
try/catch but awaited before it opened, 4223 -> 4216. 58 real hang risks
in total; the other 438 async handlers are guarded and lint-only.
A ninth typed PyHSS's REST responses via a generic pyhssApiCall, 4216 ->
4107, and surfaced three more real defects in the process.
A tenth declared the .ims-config.json state shape across its 23 parse
sites, 4107 -> 3889, turning three opaque TypeErrors into clear errors.
An eleventh typed SASBench's REST API and Kea's config JSON, 3889 -> 3778.
What is left is concentrated in the YAML config boundary, which CLAUDE.md
pattern #2 reserves for its own session, plus Phase 6's long tail.
A twelfth typed the Open5GS YAML documents (3778 -> 3533) and a thirteenth
fixed SmfSessionConfig/UpfSessionConfig, which declared a nested subnet
list no real file produces, 3533 -> 3488.
PHASE 5 IS COMPLETE as of 2026-11-26, at 2538: the YAML config boundary
closed across #82-#87 (the repository, validation, auto-config, pcap, the
APN profile, auto-assign-ips and plmn-migration), and it surfaced 16 real
defects, not one of which was itself a lint finding. Phases 6 and 7 remain.
The frontend moved 379 -> 510 on 2026-11-27, which is a WIDENED RULE SET,
not new broken code: eslint-plugin-react-hooks 4 -> 7 added the React
Compiler rules, and all 131 additions are react-hooks/*. The pre-existing
379 are all no-explicit-any.
Three of those 131 had a real defect behind them and are fixed (two
render-time ref assignments, and a chart that mutated during render), taking
the frontend to 505. The rest are fetch-on-mount effects, which this codebase
uses deliberately. Relocating four of those effects to satisfy the rule was
tried and REVERTED: a moved line is an added line to the changed-lines gate,
so it then had to satisfy the full rule set it was already failing.
The numbers recorded below are the live ones; this prose is not, so trust
the fields.
typescript-eslint 6.17 -> 8.74 on 2026-11-27 took the backend 2537 -> 2645
and the frontend 505 -> 526. That is a WIDENED RULE SET, not new broken
code, and the whole delta is accounted for rule by rule:
backend  +43 no-base-to-string (new to recommended; it catches a value
reaching a template literal or String() with no meaningful
toString, i.e. '[object Object]' in a log or an error. This
is the one class here with real-defect potential and is the
next batch worth working. 43 findings across 14 files:
radio-signal-controller.ts 11, dhcp-config.ts 6,
sip-trace-controller.ts 6, then a long tail. The six in
dhcp-config.ts matter most for their consequence rather
than their count -- that file round-trips the operator's
kea-dhcp4.conf, so a coerced value is PERSISTED.)
The six in dhcp-config.ts are FIXED (2645 -> 2639): keaStr() narrows
instead of coercing. 37 remain, radio-signal-controller.ts (11) and
sip-trace-controller.ts (6) being the next clusters.
+45 no-unnecessary-type-assertion (v8 detects more cases)
+14 no-require-imports / -5 no-var-requires (rule renamed, so
net +9 for the same findings)
+8 explicit-function-return-type, +6 no-unused-vars,
+2 no-unused-expressions, +2 prefer-promise-reject-errors,
+1 await-thenable
frontend +15 no-unused-vars (v8 defaults caughtErrors to 'all', so an
unused catch binding now counts; the config's
caughtErrorsIgnorePattern still exempts ^_)
+6 no-unused-expressions
Sampled before accepting rather than re-baselined blind. The two that
looked like real bugs were not: radio-signal-controller's is
`err ? reject(err) : resolve()`, a correct idiom flagged only because a
ternary's value is unused.
The old extends name recommended-requiring-type-checking STILL RESOLVES in
8.74 with no deprecation notice, verified against the real binary -- no
config change was needed, contrary to what the v6 deprecation note implies.
A fatal reappearing means some file is outside parserOptions.project again.
Fix the project reference; do not re-baseline around it.
PHASE 6 is the per-directory sweep. src/domain/** took 2639 -> 2560 and
found three real defects (an invented 4G/5G PLMN mismatch, a non-string SCP
URI, and four coverage rasters built with `new Array(n)`, which infers any[]
so every write into them went unchecked). src/infrastructure/network/**
then took 2560 -> 2508, all 52 findings in it, and found three more: a
private unvalidated copy of CIDR masking that returned a PLAUSIBLE wrong
network for a truncated address, an `i.ifname?.startsWith` filter that was
true for an entry with no ifname at all, and -- in ip-utils, which had no
tests until this slice -- a trailing-slash CIDR reading as the entire IPv4
space, which turned one scan loop into 4.29 billion iterations.
src/infrastructure/** then went to ZERO, 2508 -> 2345 errors and 366 -> 360
warnings across all 12 files that had findings. Five more real defects, the
two worth remembering being a WebSocket `source` field declared as a
six-way union while carrying any string the client sent (so a typo
silently returned the wrong service's logs), and a framed-routes field
holding a bare STRING instead of an array, which passed a `.length === 0`
test and was then iterated character by character into the CIDR parser.
The auth/write-guard slice (2345/360 -> 2322/359) was deliberately NOT a
lint slice. It went looking for one class of thing -- places where the
compiler had been told something untrue -- and the lint movement is a side
effect of three real defects. `POST /api/autoconfig/start` carried no admin
guard, measured against 340 write routes that did and 24 others that are
deliberately open; a viewer could re-address the NIC, write a netplan
drop-in, install thirteen modules and restart the core. The session
middleware was an async function with no try/catch, and express is pinned at
4.x, which does not forward a rejected async-middleware promise to its error
handler -- with no unhandledRejection handler anywhere, one SQLITE_BUSY on
any authenticated request terminated the backend. And `createLucia`'s second
generic named the snake_case database row rather than what
`getUserAttributes` returns, which is why callers reached for
`(user as any).createdAt` to read a field that genuinely exists -- reverting
that one generic reproduces both casts as compile errors.
write-route-admin-guard.test.ts is the part worth copying. It enumerates the
routes from source and requires every unguarded one to be allow-listed with
a stated reason, so a viewer-reachable write route becomes a decision
somebody wrote down rather than an omission nobody measured.
The same slice added middleware/async-handler.ts. It is one `.catch(next)`,
and it makes index.ts's existing express error handler — which already
handles the headersSent case the streaming /install endpoints create —
reachable from an async rejection, which on express 4 it never was. Applied
to rf-planning-projects-controller.ts only, because the changed-lines gate
held the five route lines this slice touched to their pre-existing
no-misused-promises findings and the honest fix was the wrapper rather than
a disable. That is the idiom for the interfaces/rest slice: 451 findings of
this rule remain, and measurement says they are lint-only (all 434 async
handlers carry their own try/catch), so the wrapper is a net under the
floor, not a substitute for one.
2026-11-27 (rest-unguarded-sync): 2322 -> 2302. Not a lint pass: 15 async
route handlers that do throwing sync work outside their own try were
wrapped in asyncHandler, which happens to clear 19 no-misused-promises
findings as a side effect. express 4 does not forward a rejected handler
promise to its error handler and this process installs no
unhandledRejection listener, so each was a path where one disk error
exits the backend. Pinned by unguarded-sync-work.test.ts.
To lower the counts after real cleanup:
cd backend && npm run -s lint:json | node ../scripts/lint-ratchet.mjs backend --update
